paper/frame_caption.text:
Inspect ONE image from the current segment. The image is primary evidence; the original caption is a hypothesis.
Observe the interacting foreground entities and stable visible anchors separately, including simultaneously present tools, containers, hands, fabric, food and surfaces. Use broad labels when a subtype is uncertain. Do not assign anatomical hand sides. Record states, not an imagined action sequence.
Do not assert a liquid source unless a stream from that source is visible. Do not infer preparation versus serving, hidden intent, past/future events or off-screen causes. Preserve readable text literally; uncertain text is not a fact.
Give a 1-2 sentence factual caption, observations, uncertainties and unsupported_original_claims. Also return frame_id and entities.
Each entity has a frame-local ID E0, E1, etc.; IDs do NOT establish identity across frames. Give a label, broad category, concrete appearance_cues, visible_state, position, uncertainties and evidence_refs.
position.region uses exactly one of: upper_left, upper_center, upper_right, center_left, center, center_right, lower_left, lower_center, lower_right, uncertain. Coordinates refer to the IMAGE.
position.anchor_entity is another listed entity ID or null. position.relation uses exactly one of: inside, above, below, image_left_of, image_right_of, on, touching, overlapping, near, none, uncertain. Use null with none/uncertain, and a listed anchor with any other relation. position.certain is false for unresolved placement. A utensil may overlap a container without becoming the container.
Use the actual dominant location of an entity, with its interaction specified relative to a stable anchor. Do not merge a pot, a spoon and a cloth into one entity.
category uses exactly one of: person, body_part, container, utensil, fabric, food, surface, text, other.
Return STRICT JSON with this structure (fill actual observations; no schema placeholders):
{"frame_id":"$frame_id","caption":"...","observations":["..."],"uncertainties":[],"unsupported_original_claims":[],"entities":[{"entity_id":"E0","label":"...","category":"other","appearance_cues":["..."],"visible_state":"...","position":{"region":"center","anchor_entity":null,"relation":"none","certain":true},"uncertainties":[],"evidence_refs":["${frame_id}_IMAGE"]}]}
FRAME: $frame_id
ORIGINAL CAPTION: $original_caption
RELATION CONTRACT: For every entity add spatial_relations (an empty list when none is established). Keep the existing position field and set position.reference_frame="image". The position region and primary relation do not exhaust the entity's relations and cannot exclude another axis. For an interacting entity record each supported horizontal/vertical/contact relation independently:
{"axis":"horizontal|vertical|contact","anchor_entity":"another actual local E ID","reference_frame":"image","subject_part":"concrete entity part, or whole","anchor_part":"concrete anchor part, or whole","relation":"allowed value","certain":true|false,"support":"concrete visible cues and the comparison basis","evidence_refs":["${frame_id}_IMAGE"]}.
Allowed relations: horizontal=image_left_of/image_right_of/overlapping/uncertain; vertical=above/below/overlapping/uncertain; contact=touching/on/inside/none/uncertain. Describe whether a left/right statement uses a center offset or entire extents; a left-offset center does not mean no horizontal overlap. Above a left portion and left-offset may coexist. State actual visible part/anchor extents; do not invent exact bounding boxes, coordinates, 3D depth or contact from projection. Missing relation evidence is unknown, not a negative fact. Use uncertain/certain=false where needed.
For body_part entities also add role as a concrete held/contacted-object role. Keep hand/arm role and IMAGE placement distinct from a person's anatomical left/right. Do not assign an anatomical side or expand a role into hidden intent. Describe each object's own state: a handle covering is not an opening covering; overlap does not establish a liquid source.

VISUAL PRECISION: Distinguish an object's supported holding/manipulation role from the exact occluded material-contact interface. Visible grasp posture, a handle segment and the supported object's arrangement can establish holding even when fingers or cloth hide the precise contact surfaces. Describe supported roles and their cues; keep the hidden interface uncertain. Do not require every contact surface to be visible, and do not negate holding merely because that interface is occluded. Conversely mere proximity without such cues does not establish a hold.
Use above/over/left/right for grounded image-plane placement unless the wording explicitly asserts physical depth or contact. Qualitative relations and explicitly approximate image estimates do not require measured annotations. Check the estimate's broad consistency; do not treat approximate as exact.
paper/frame_caption.adaptations: Structured image-bound entity states extend Fig.13 without replacing the existing caption contract; observation structure is not visual acceptance; v8 independent spatial axes and body-part roles / claim and answer checks; v11 separates supported manipulation roles from occluded exact contact

t3_local/pair_transition.text:
Compare images A -> B in this direction. Images are primary evidence. The supplied frame observations are imperfect pixel observations, not ground truth. Check them against both images. Captions, summary and tool signals cannot establish a change absent from the images.
First match the SAME entities by concrete shape, appearance and visible relationships. Local E IDs are independently assigned per frame: identical ID numbers do not prove identity. Distinguish tools, containers, fabric, body parts and food. A cloth and a spoon can both persist; moving a tool is not replacing another object. If identity is unresolved use status uncertain and do not create an edit on that match.
Account for EVERY listed entity once, either in matches or unmatched_source/unmatched_target. Matches are one-to-one. status uses same or uncertain; provide identity_cues and both image evidence IDs. A same match must have compatible broad categories.
Then compare each supported source state with its destination state, especially tool positions relative to visible containers/food/surfaces. Explicitly inspect position differences even when captions describe the same ongoing activity. If supplied positions disagree with pixels, mark that match uncertain, explain the observation error, and do not silently assert no change.
Describe meaningful visible appearance/disappearance, movement, rotation, state, exact readable text, camera/view or shot changes. Ignore insignificant artifacts. An unseen object is not proof of physical destruction; unmatched does not automatically mean add/remove. Do not infer pouring, preparation/serving, hidden intent or future steps.
Each change has source_entity, target_entity, verb, source_state, target_state, edit and evidence_refs for BOTH images. Movement/state edits need a same match. add uses source_entity=null and an unmatched target; remove uses an unmatched source and target_entity=null. Camera/shot edits use both entity IDs null. Each entity edit must use the supplied source entity label (the target label for add), so its target is explicit.
Allowed verbs: add, remove, move, rotate, open, close, turn on, turn off, change text, zoom, pan, tilt, cut. An edit has one target and one verb. Describe A and B image-coordinate positions; never anatomical hand sides. Prefer camera verbs when viewpoint explains motion. Changes do not automatically qualify as 1-2 small controllable edits.
transition keeps the paper format: Edits(k): 1) ...; 2) ... | Shot: <none/minor/scene_cut> | View: <none/minor/major> | Subject: <same/unclear/different> | Uncertainty: <none or a note>.
Its edits MUST exactly match changes[].edit in order, and k must equal their count. A shot boundary needs cut to new shot. For no supported meaningful change use changes=[], Edits(0): none, and a concrete no_change_reason comparing the states. A clear matched position difference cannot coexist with no-change. Unknown change is uncertainty, not an invented edit.
Return ONLY STRICT JSON:
{"source_frame":"...","target_frame":"...","matches":[{"source_entity":"E0","target_entity":"E1","status":"same","identity_cues":["..."],"evidence_refs":["F00_IMAGE","F01_IMAGE"]}],"unmatched_source":[],"unmatched_target":[],"changes":[{"source_entity":"E0","target_entity":"E1","verb":"move","source_state":"...","target_state":"...","edit":"move <actual entity label> from <A position> to <B position>","evidence_refs":["F00_IMAGE","F01_IMAGE"]}],"no_change_reason":null,"uncertainties":[],"transition":"..."}
The example IDs illustrate the schema only; use the actual supplied frame IDs and entities.
Video type: $video_type
Segment background: $summary
Modality advice: $advice
Secondary captions A: $cap_a; B: $cap_b
OBSERVATIONS A: $states_a
OBSERVATIONS B: $states_b
Also compare independently established spatial_relations on matching axes, subject parts and stable anchor parts. Do not infer a not-above fact from horizontal image-left placement. Check relation changes directly against pixels, with their uncertainty and actual reference frame. An absent axis is unknown. Do not invent exact trajectories between images or anatomical hand-side labels. Maintain object-role identity.
t3_local/pair_transition.adaptations: Explicit one-to-one entity matching and state-to-transition consistency; JSON audit envelope retains the paper transition string interface; v8 independent spatial axes and body-part roles / claim and answer checks

paper/signal_filter.text:
You are a precise semantic filtering assistant.
Filter each supplied semantic tool signal by its associated shot summary and frame caption.
Keep only clearly supported, relevant, useful signals. Remove irrelevant, redundant, vague, unsupported, inconsistent or weakly related signals; remove if uncertain.
Treat tools as imperfect auxiliary evidence. ASR is nearby speech, not visible text. Motion magnitude is not an action or importance label.
Do not invent, rewrite or merge signals. Preserve exact OCR wording, spelling, numbers and newlines in retained evidence.
Return STRICT JSON: {"retained": [{"id": "...", "reason": "..."}], "removed": [{"id": "...", "reason": "..."}]}.
Classify every supplied ID exactly once.
SHOTS: $shots_json
SIGNALS: $signals_json
paper/signal_filter.adaptations: Stable signal IDs and immutable wording instead of returning rewritten signal strings; caption context included

paper/gate_c.text:
You are a strict metadata-level admission judge for video-to-dataset generation.
Judge the whole package using summaries, captions, retained tool signals and consecutive transitions. Check factual claims against the supplied images.
This metadata describes only the current input SEGMENT.
Apply ALL seven criteria:
1. Grounded visual content: concrete visible entities, interactions, states, layouts, readable text or meaningful changes.
2. Cross-level coherence: summaries, captions, images and transitions agree; a plausible summary cannot override contradictory image evidence.
3. Dataset usefulness: enough support for at least one meaningful understanding, editing or unified task.
4. Evidence density: distinct specific evidence; reject generic filler and uninformative near-duplicates.
5. Tool reliability: tools are auxiliary; unsupported or contradictory signals cannot establish a fact.
6. Temporal/structural value: meaningful progression, interactions, procedures, layouts or object relations. Static informative content can support understanding.
7. Hallucination safety: reject metadata requiring invented identities, exact text, hidden causes, intentions, unobserved stage contrasts or future events.
Distinguish held containers, interacting tools and visible liquid flow. Do not infer a pouring source merely from a held pot.
Judge raw image quality only when it prevents metadata grounding.
A transition explicitly marked call_failed or invalid is incomplete evidence, not a claim of no change; reject the incomplete package.
Return STRICT JSON: {"decision": "accept" or "reject", "primary_reasons": [2-4 concise reasons], "summary_consistent": true or false}.
Reject if summary_consistent is false.
METADATA: $metadata_json
Only the reviewed claims supplied in this package are judged. Earlier captions and summaries retained elsewhere are pre-verification hypotheses, not current claims. Uncertainty notes do not assert that an event occurred.
Inspect the structured entities and every cross-frame match directly against the images. Contract-valid is not visually approved. Check persistent tools/containers/fabric, source and target positions, and omitted visible changes. Do not accept a no-change assertion merely because captions repeat. Reject a package with materially false entity states or unexplained missing changes; uncertainty may remain when it does not undermine the supported tasks.
Return claim_checks in the exact metadata order: all keyframes by frame_id, then all transitions by transition_id. Each row must contain {"id":"actual Fxx/Txx ID","entities_supported":true|false,"relations_supported":true|false,"direction_supported":true|false,"uncertainty_preserved":true|false,"reason":"concrete independent image support or precise contradiction"}. For an inapplicable field use true and explain it. Check all materially asserted relations, including primary positions, typed horizontal/vertical/contact relations and free-text states. A relation on one axis does not exclude a relation on another axis. Inspect the actual object part and anchor part; do not treat a center offset as separation of the entire extents or a 2D projection as proof of depth/contact. A summary that drops a materially changed relation cannot override the frame observations. Independently follow each ordered pair; do not import a later movement into earlier context. Body-part roles do not establish anatomical left/right. Accept requires every claim check to pass; unresolved relations must remain uncertain without asserting their negations. A previous metadata approval is not evidence.

For every claim_checks row also return entities_complete:true|false. Compare visible interacting objects and held/contacted body-part roles against the actual inventory, not merely the listed claims. An omitted critical entity or a missing task-relevant relation must not escape review by never being asserted. For transitions entities_complete checks whether the relevant visible participants and their identity/roles are accounted for. Accept requires complete task-relevant coverage, coherent free text and typed relations, as well as all previous checks. Unchanged background is still a hypothesis to verify; a localized patch is not prior approval.

VISUAL PRECISION: Distinguish an object's supported holding/manipulation role from the exact occluded material-contact interface. Visible grasp posture, a handle segment and the supported object's arrangement can establish holding even when fingers or cloth hide the precise contact surfaces. Describe supported roles and their cues; keep the hidden interface uncertain. Do not require every contact surface to be visible, and do not negate holding merely because that interface is occluded. Conversely mere proximity without such cues does not establish a hold.
Use above/over/left/right for grounded image-plane placement unless the wording explicitly asserts physical depth or contact. Qualitative relations and explicitly approximate image estimates do not require measured annotations. Check the estimate's broad consistency; do not treat approximate as exact.

For each keyframe explicitly inspect all interacting hands and held objects, not only the last frame. Missing body-part role or missing spatial_relations for task-relevant interacting objects is incomplete observation even if the caption sounds plausible. Preserve valid uncertainty within explicit relations.
paper/gate_c.adaptations: Explicit visual summary verification and segment scope; distinguishes failed observations from no change; checks structured observations and identity matches against pixels; v8 independent spatial axes and body-part roles / claim and answer checks; v9 independently checks task-relevant entity/relation completeness; v11 separates supported manipulation roles from occluded exact contact

paper/routing.text:
You are a quota allocator for dataset instance generation.
Route the reviewed segment to the NINE paper task types. Multiple types may be suitable.
Use ONLY the EVIDENCE PACK; tools are imperfect auxiliary evidence. Read S_SEGEMENT_SUM before concrete frame/transition evidence.
For every task give quota, reason, evidence_refs. Positive quota requires an existing S_* ID and relevant frame/transition IDs. Explain zero quotas.
Use zero when support is insufficient; do not infer hidden causes or fill quotas with trivial questions.
fine_grained_perception: visible single-image entities, attributes, relations or text, with a unique MCQ answer.
single_image_reasoning: a visible-cue-supported inference about interaction, function or constraints, not an unknown stage or hidden intent.
multi_image_logic: at least two images with useful cross-image comparison or joint verification.
localized_editing and grounded_edit_to_select: only supplied reviewed pairs with 1-2 small controllable atomic edits.
understand_recall_generate_select: recall of a previously shown later detail and meaningful earlier-to-later change.
stepwise_sequence and middle_step_gap: coherent distinct ordered states and supported adjacent changes.
instructional_future_sequence: at least two context states and real, grounded immediate future states.
Temporal tasks require semantic state changes, not camera-only motion, cuts or redundant frames; they do not all require a MagicBrush edit pair.
ELIGIBLE flags are feasibility limits, not instructions to select every eligible task. Set zero if false; do not exceed limits.
TASKS: $tasks_json
LIMITS: $limits_json
ELIGIBLE: $eligible_json
REVIEWED EDIT PAIRS (keyframe positions): $pairs_json
EVIDENCE PACK:
$evidence_text
Return STRICT JSON: {"tasks": {"task_name": {"quota": 0, "reason": "...", "evidence_refs": []}}, "edit_pairs": [{"from": 0, "to": 1}]}.
Include all nine task names; choose pairs only from the supplied list.
Multi-image comparison of changing object positions/relations is itself useful under Appendix D; it does not require a food-state change, hidden cause or uniquely inferred action. Inspect actual grounded comparison opportunities, while remaining free to choose quota zero with an evidence-based reason.
Weave recalls a previously shown LATER detail from EARLIER input plus prior dialogue history, not an earlier detail from a new later image.
Instructional future tasks separate ordered context states from real future targets. Do not count every available frame as context or invent a future action from tool handling. For a three-state sequence the first two are context and the third is the future reference; target supervision is not a solver observation.
paper/routing.adaptations: Nine explicit template routes replace legacy benchmark quotas; task-specific temporal eligibility; quality before output count; v10 explicit cross-image comparison and recall/context-future definitions

t4_structured/llava_answer_rules.text:
LLaVA answer rules:
- Use 2-4 sentences: a supported conclusion followed by concrete visible cues.
- Do not mention evidence IDs or tools in training text.
- Do not infer unsupported details, hidden intent, future events or an unobserved preparation/serving stage.
- Use image-frame spatial positions, never anatomical laterality.
t4_structured/llava_answer_rules.adaptations: Unifies answer length with the paper

t4_structured/llava_reasoning_rules.text:
Visual reasoning rules:
- Require reasoning about visible interaction, function, constraint-based identification, image-frame spatial relations or an observable inconsistency.
- The question premise and any contrast MUST be supported by this image alone.
- Never ask why an unobserved alternative is not happening, infer a hidden intention, or guess what happened before or will happen next.
- If support is insufficient, return fewer items, including an empty items list.
- Identify the target clearly and justify the conclusion with relevant visible cues. Generic scene context is not proof of a specific causal claim.
- The answer follows the 2-4 sentence rule; do not impose another length requirement.
- Return reasoning_evidence: conclusion, visible_cues, inference_link, answer_claims.
- Each visible_cues entry has claim and same-image evidence_refs. inference_link explains how those visible cues support an inference beyond directly naming/describing the scene. This explanation is not itself evidence.
- answer_claims must cover EVERY answer sentence verbatim, in order; each has claim, support (visible or inferred), evidence_refs. Inferred claims must follow from the stated visible cues. No hidden stage, intent or unseen event.
- A category label or extra sentence does not turn a direct action description into reasoning. Return no item when no substantive supported inference exists.

Check the question's premises and every answer sentence. A hedge such as likely does not supply evidence for an unseen transfer, stage or intention. If no visible cue distinguishes the claimed purpose from other compatible purposes, withhold that item rather than assert the most likely purpose. Do not repair a failed question by changing its object, purpose or temporal role.

Grounded function reasoning can use common-sense physical knowledge together with concrete same-image cues. A barrier/grip/insulation function can be supported without visible heat or directly measured force. Explain the cue-to-function inference and qualify inferred conditions; do not assert a hidden contact interface, actual temperature, transfer, intent or stage as observed. A likely function is not a license to invent a likely purpose of an unseen event. Preserve the original question's object and purpose when reviewing it.
t4_structured/llava_reasoning_rules.adaptations: Removes unsupported intent/stage inference and conflicting two-sentence constraint; author exposes visible cues, inference link and every answer claim for independent semantic review; v10 complete sentence-level solver scope and premise support

t4_generation_prompts/fewshot_bank/llava.adaptations: Visible function example replaces prediction of leaving a place; legacy category preserved with paper semantic category

t4_structured/single_image_rules.text:
Single-image rules:
- A solver sees ONLY the image at that item's image_pos.
- Use only the corresponding Fxx_* evidence to establish the answer. S_* is light background only.
- Other frames, transitions, ASR or segment progression cannot supply a fact absent from this image.
- Cite at least one original frame evidence ID for the same image_pos.
- No before/after/earlier/later/next/previous, invisible stage/intent, or future-event premises.
- Return fewer items if support is insufficient. Do not turn uncertainty into an assertion.
t4_structured/single_image_rules.adaptations: Explicit per-item evidence scope and abstention

t4_structured/mmt_option_rules.text:
MMT multiple-choice rules (SINGLE-CORRECT HARD):
- Provide exactly ONE correct option; the other 3 must be plausible distractors.
- All options must be the SAME type/granularity (all colors / all object types / all counts / etc.).
- Distractors should be wrong by ONE key visual detail, not random.
- Keep options similar length/style. No "All of the above" / "None of the above".

COUNTING POLICY (HARD — because exact counting is error-prone):
- DO NOT ask exact-count questions by default.
- You may ask an exact-count question ONLY if ALL conditions hold:
  (1) The target set is CLOSED: "fully visible in-frame" AND clearly belongs to the set.
  (2) Objects are NOT occluded and do NOT extend out of frame.
  (3) The correct count is in {0,1,2} ONLY.
  (4) The question explicitly states viewpoint reference if using left/right: "from the camera viewpoint".
- If ANY condition is not satisfied, replace with a MORE ROBUST alternative:
  * comparison
  * threshold
  * identification instead of count

UNIQUENESS CHECK (HARD, internal only):
- The correct option must be uniquely true.
- If 2+ options could be true due to ambiguity, you MUST fix it by rewriting:
  (a) tighten the question with extra anchors, OR
  (b) rewrite options so only ONE matches the image.
- Do this internally; output ONLY the final JSON.
- Distractors must be mutually exclusive for THIS question; synonyms and subset/superset answers can make more than one option true.
- A held object does not establish it as the source of a visible action. Verify the action premise.
- Return fewer items or none if uniqueness cannot be established without changing the task.
Return perception_evidence with premise_cues (claim and same-image evidence_refs) and option_checks for A/B/C/D. Each option check has status supported/excluded/uncertain, reason and same-image evidence_refs. Exactly the answer option must be supported; each distractor must have a concrete exclusion reason. If two options overlap or a premise is not visible, withhold the item. The evidence contract does not replace visual review.

Check spatial options independently: right/left versus behind/in-front belong to different axes and can both hold. Do not use mixed-axis options unless the question defines an exclusive category supported by the image. Do not silently reinterpret the question to manufacture uniqueness.
t4_structured/mmt_option_rules.adaptations: Clarifies overlapping options and unsupported action premises; explicit premise and per-option evidence contract; cross-axis spatial overlap

t4_structured/mmt_verifier.text:
You are verifying MMT multiple-choice questions for SINGLE-IMAGE evaluation.
Goal: reduce ambiguity and ensure EXACTLY ONE correct option.

Hard rules (MUST follow):
- Each item is answerable from ONLY the image at image_pos.
- There MUST be exactly ONE correct option among A/B/C/D.
- Options must be same type/granularity; no multi-attribute mixes.
- Question must be unambiguous: the target must be uniquely anchored (type + disambiguation anchor).
- Do NOT use timeline/sequence language (before/after/earlier/later/next/previous).
- Do NOT invent details beyond evidence.

- category MUST be one of: $mmt_allowed_categories_json.
- l2-category MUST be one of: $mmt_allowed_l2_json.

- If an item uses anatomical/person-relative left/right (e.g., "person's left hand"), you MUST NOT convert it to image-left/right.
- You may only fix it by rewriting into a screen-position description WITHOUT claiming anatomical side,
  e.g., "the hand visible on the left side of the image" + one extra anchor.
- If you cannot fix without semantic change or invention, set ok=false.

What you can do:
- If the item is already good: ok=true, fixed_item can be omitted or identical.
- If ambiguous but fixable: ok=true and provide fixed_item with minimal edits.
- If not fixable without inventing: ok=false.

OUTPUT STRICT JSON ONLY in this schema:
{
  "results": [
    {
      "ok": true,
      "reason": "",
      "fixed_item": {
        "image_pos": 0,
        "category": "",
        "l2-category": "",
        "question": "",
        "A": "",
        "B": "",
        "C": "",
        "D": "",
        "_answer": "",
        "evidence_refs": []
      }
    }
  ]
}

INPUT ITEMS:
$payload_json

EVIDENCE PACK:
$evidence_pack_text
Additional paper rules: preserve image_pos, question object, requested attribute and task purpose. Never invent a fix or substitute an easier question. Synonym/subset options must not both be true. If text evidence cannot establish the premise or uniqueness, set ok=false. This is a TEXT check, not proof of image correctness.
Preserve perception_evidence verbatim when returning fixed_item. Do not rewrite the question, options, answer or evidence to make a failed task pass; reject unresolved semantic changes.
t4_structured/mmt_verifier.adaptations: Intent-preserving text verification; unresolved visual support rejects

umm_task_prompts/benchmark_style_rules.text:
Shared paper task rules:
- Author the complete task for the Appendix D round contract, not only a recognition or selection question.
- All textual answers must be supported by the supplied captions/transitions; keep entity, direction and target identity stable.
- Every output must contain original evidence_refs selected from the pack; cite the actual endpoint frames and transitions used.
- Every select.answer is exactly target:FXX for the supplied real target, and its rationale explains unique support.
- Do not speculate about hidden causes or invent intermediate/future images.
- Author-side access to target evidence is allowed. Solver-side image inputs follow the round contract and must not contain an unobserved future target.
umm_task_prompts/benchmark_style_rules.adaptations: Complete task semantics and mandatory original citations; author/solver scope distinction

umm_task_prompts/seed_system_style.text: Author a grounded edit-to-generate-and-select task. The source and target define real local visible changes. The plan supports target-image generation; selection checks the generated result.

umm_task_prompts/seed_extra_rules.text:
SEED contract: Plan -> Gen -> Select.
plan.goal describes the target; invariants name unchanged visible content; edits cover the supplied reviewed 1-2 atomic changes.
gen.summary describes that target state. Gen solver image input is source only after the plan.
select chooses the supplied target among real candidates; cite both endpoint captions and the reviewed change.
Never add an unobserved edit or omit a supported target change.
umm_task_prompts/seed_extra_rules.adaptations: Keeps existing internal schema and renderer

umm_task_prompts/weave_extra_rules.text:
Weave contract: Understand -> Plan -> QA -> Gen -> Select.
understand.facts includes concrete earlier and later facts; plan.edits connects them.
qa_open tests a specific detail of the previously shown later image. Its current image input is earlier only, and its answer/rubric bind to the later detail seen in the preceding dialogue.
Preserve the question object and requested attribute; background recall must not be converted into an edit/action question.
Gen recalls the later state; select chooses that same target. A temporal visual change need not satisfy MagicBrush editing limits.
Cite both endpoint captions and the transition supporting the plan.
There is no universal 1-2-edit limit for Weave. Use complete verified entity states and comparisons; keep pot/container, tool and hand distinct. Do not convert object displacement into pouring without observed flow.
umm_task_prompts/weave_extra_rules.adaptations: Explicit recall ordering and intent; removes universal edited-pair constraint; explicit separate edit-count contract

umm_task_prompts/comm_c1_extra_rules.text:
CoMM C1 contract: Overall -> Steps -> Gen for each step -> Select for each step.
Use one coherent observed visual sequence; each step_text describes its supplied adjacent transition and target state.
Keep step_texts/select lengths equal to the actual transition count, preserve order, and keep entity/style identity consistent.
Each Gen uses the preceding step state; select[i] targets the corresponding supplied next state.
Do not invent steps, require all transitions to be MagicBrush edits, or repeat an unchanged state as progression.
Cite all used frame captions and adjacent transitions.
The overall answer is solved from ONLY the first and last supplied images, with no earlier conversation containing intermediate frames. Describe endpoint-supported change; do not narrate a hidden middle-state detour or reversal. Detailed intermediate actions belong only in step_texts. The author sees all frames but must not leak that privilege into overall.
This request authors only question, step_texts and select. Do not return overall; a separate endpoint-only request authors that field. Keep the same entity-tracking purpose and preserve the complete observed step sequence.
Distinguish a cloth-covered handle from a covered pot opening; use anchored image-side hand roles without unverified anatomical labels.
umm_task_prompts/comm_c1_extra_rules.adaptations: Observed progression and explicit lengths/targets; endpoint-only overall claims; separate endpoint-only overall author

umm_task_prompts/comm_c2_extra_rules.text:
C2 contract: Explain -> Gen -> Select. The target remains the actual observed middle frame and must fit both supplied adjacent transitions. The author sees all three frames; the Explain/Gen solver sees only the endpoints.
Write explanation as a constructive description of a compatible middle state and its endpoint-supported continuity. Do not claim the solver directly observed the hidden middle image, quote its exact hidden motion trace, or state that endpoints uniquely determine every intermediate detail. Describe the actual middle target as the state to reconstruct; check its visible compatibility with both endpoints. Preserve entities, target, task purpose and selection binding.
Use image-coordinate anchors, no unsupported anatomy, intention, food identity or pouring. Select chooses the real middle candidate consistent with that reconstruction. Return all three frame CAP citations and both adjacent TRANS citations; summary is optional context.
Use the bound hand/arm roles and explicit image coordinates. Do not translate viewer-side placement or object-role labels into anatomical left/right. Preserve the same reconstruction purpose and the actual reference middle state; do not substitute an easier target or claim observation of a hidden trajectory. Check every explanation claim before emitting it.

Every clause describing the hidden middle or its approach/departure must remain explicitly constructive: a compatible middle could place ..., followed by ... to reach the visible endpoint. Do not narrate exact hidden movements as observed facts before qualifying the final sentence. Do not quote middle pixel coordinates; the solver only sees endpoints at Explain/Gen. Describe the actual reference middle as a state to reconstruct, preserving its entities, roles, adjacent-transition compatibility and selection binding. Check every sentence separately for solver scope.

Write a short constructive explanation: (1) a compatible middle could show the actual target configuration; (2) a plausible approach could connect the visible start to that proposed state, and a plausible departure could connect it to the visible end. ALL hidden approach/departure clauses must remain hypothetical. Do not say observed F01, recorded F00->F01 motion, or the middle target therefore is observed. Do not include hidden coordinates. Actual adjacent transition citations remain author provenance; they are not events the endpoint-only solver saw. Selection rationale can describe the shown middle candidate after generation, but cannot retroactively assert prior observation.

umm_task_prompts/isg_extra_rules.text:
ISG contract: Overall -> Edit -> Reason -> Target -> Check -> Gen for each future step -> Select.
Use the supplied two context states and real future targets. edits/because/so_that/check/select have exactly the future-step count.
Each edit describes the corresponding immediate future transition, not the context transition. Reasons describe visible continuity, not hidden intent or unseen causes.
Each target and check describes observable conditions of that future frame.
Gen i can see context and previously generated states only, never the current or later future image.
Cite context/target captions and the adjacent transitions used. These are observed temporal states, not necessarily small controllable MagicBrush edits.
The overall answer is an instruction for a compatible continuation from the shown context, not a statement that the solver has already observed the hidden future target. Phrase edits as instructions and so_that as the desired visual conditions. because must cite concrete continuity/constraints visible in the context or previously generated states; never use a hidden future image as an observed causal premise or infer human purpose. Keep the real supplied target, immediate temporal direction and candidate bindings. A target instruction need not claim that its future is uniquely deducible, but it must be a coherent continuation from the context rather than an arbitrary unrelated change. Cite every context/target CAP and adjacent TRANS supplied for this sequence.
Separate OBSERVED CONTEXT facts from DESIRED FUTURE conditions in every sentence. The future reference is author supervision, not a next observed state shown to the solver. Do not infer a plating/preparation/serving purpose from generic tool handling. Reasons must use the shown context's own ordered movement, never the direction of the withheld future target. Instructions may construct a compatible grounded continuation without claiming it already happened or uniquely follows. Keep independent spatial axes and anchored hand roles; check every target and selection against the actual reference.

For each because entry, name only an observed context constraint or a continuity condition of the previously stated instruction; do not say the next visible transition already occurs or cite a hidden future transition as observed evidence. Keep context transition IDs distinct from future transition IDs. A desired continuation may reverse the context's motion, but do not claim that reversal is observed or uniquely predicted. State why the proposed target remains spatially compatible with the shown context. Keep the real future target, its direction and all generation/selection bindings. Each sentence must distinguish observed context from requested future.

Audit selection rationales as well as planning clauses. Preserve the supplied global transition IDs exactly: use the actual from/to pair attached to each ID; never renumber a future transition locally as P00 just because it is the first future step. A selection rationale should cite concrete candidate/target features and the already supplied desired instruction. Do not attribute a desired-future direction to a different context transition. When a citation is unnecessary in prose, omit it rather than guessing its ID; keep required evidence_refs intact.
umm_task_prompts/isg_extra_rules.adaptations: Array/target/temporal scope requirements; context-supported reasons and desired future instructions, not hidden observations; v8 independent spatial axes and body-part roles / claim and answer checks; v10 complete sentence-level solver scope and premise support

paper/visual_review.text:
Independently solve and review the supplied task using the same original images. Candidate prose is a proposal, not evidence. Selection keys and rationale are withheld until your independent answers are frozen.
The compact input contains each exact sentence once in claims, plus every occurrence's original source and round. Round queries/answers refer to those ids. Check all factual clauses and ALL occurrences; a fact valid in a reviewer target can still be unsupported in an earlier solver round. Query image labels are local to that query; review_image_bindings maps your supplied images to global positions. Follow each actual round's images and previously shown history, not all reviewer images as solver context.
Independent observations were collected before the candidate and are fallible. Inspect pixels directly. A missing observation is not negative evidence. If pixels contradict an observation, report the concrete discrepancy and withhold approval; do not silently pick the candidate wording.
Distinguish a supported holding/manipulation role from its hidden exact contact interface. Grasp posture, visible handle and supported arrangement may establish holding even if cloth/fingers hide the interface. Proximity alone does not establish holding. Keep horizontal, vertical, depth and contact separate using named parts. Horizontal offset can coexist with above placement or partial projection overlap. Tilt/unknown contents do not establish pouring. Do not assert unseen food identity, transfer, temperature, stage, intention or future as an observed fact.
Coordinates: use the explicit original dimensions and units below. Observation boxes are approximate normalized 0..1000; candidate point estimates may use original pixels. They describe different parts/extents and cannot be compared as equal measurements. Verify broad directional/positional consistency against pixels. Unspecified units remain uncertain. Qualitative placement does not require measured labels.
APPLICABLE TASK CONTRACT (apply this block only):
$task_contract
Open descriptions and constructive generation can have multiple supported phrasings/completions. unique_answer/options_exclusive are true schema conventions for open rounds; actual selection rounds still require exactly one supported option and all other options excluded. Do not apply the single-image reasoning inference requirement to other task types. Desired target states are assessed for compatibility and target match, not as claims that the solver observed or uniquely predicted them.
Return one STRICT JSON object following this complete schema. Fill all rows and fields even on hold/reject. Booleans shown below are placeholders, not judgments. supported/contradicted claim checks require actual observation ids; not_applicable is only a pure request with no visual assertion, never an answer. Check every occurrence's solver scope. Each select round supplies exactly its shown option letters with independent reasons; each open/generation round supplies your own supported assessment. For inapplicable round booleans use true and explain. Accept requires every premise, factual clause, target/direction and applicable task contract to pass with no unresolved uncertainty.
RESPONSE SCHEMA:
$response_schema
COMPACT INPUT:
$projection_json
paper/visual_review.adaptations: Compact per-round text references, parsed observations once, explicit coordinate units, one task-specific contract and one complete response schema; no candidate edits.

chapter_summary_generation.text:
You are a robust chapter summarizer for a structured video understanding pipeline.

A chapter summary must summarize the full meaning of one chapter by integrating all shot summaries that belong to that chapter.
The output should describe the chapter as a coherent local segment of the video, not as disconnected bullet points.

Your task:
- Read all provided shot summaries for this chapter.
- Merge them into one concise, fluent, informative English paragraph.
- Preserve the important subject matter, actions, stages, transitions, or outcomes that define the chapter.
- Remove redundancy and avoid repeating nearly identical wording from multiple shots.
- If the chapter contains multiple steps or states, reflect that progression naturally in the summary.
- Stay grounded in the provided shot summaries only. Do not invent details.

Writing requirements:
- Write plain English only.
- Output exactly one short paragraph.
- Do not use bullet points, numbering, JSON, markdown, labels, or quotation marks around the answer.
- Keep the summary compact but specific.
- Prefer a summary that is easy for downstream planning, scoring, and visualization to read.

Return the chapter summary only.
Scope clarification: the original video may have been cut into fixed-length input segments. Here video/global means ONLY the current input segment, not the unsupplied full source video. Do not infer events outside that segment.

A comparison can report the absence of an expected condition when the evidence supports that absence. Do not infer preparation/serving stage, intention, food identity or a hidden action. Return fewer dialogues or none when the requested task cannot be grounded.

paper/observation_patch.text:
Inspect this ONE image. The supplied observation is an imperfect hypothesis, not truth.
Preserve the inventory and frame-local IDs. Inspect the focus entities and their interactions directly in the image. Do not replace, add, remove, rename, retype or reorder entities. Use anchored held-object roles and IMAGE coordinates, never anatomical left/right. Inspect each object's own parts separately: body, opening, handle and covering are different. Use broad existing labels rather than inventing a subtype, intent, stage, hidden source or trajectory.
For each focus entity explicitly check identity, held/contacted-object role, own visible state, and supported relations to the existing anchors. Keep horizontal, vertical and contact axes independent. Left-offset centers may coexist with horizontal overlap and above an anchor portion; missing axes are unknown. Projection does not prove depth/contact. Do not invent coordinates. Supported relations must identify subject_part, anchor_part and the visible comparison basis. For hands record role; for interacting objects record spatial_relations including uncertainty rather than omit an unresolved important relation.
Return only a localized patch. Allowed entity fields: visible_state, position, spatial_relations, role, uncertainties. Allowed frame fields: caption, observations, uncertainties, unsupported_original_claims. before contains the exact current values of every updated field (null for an absent optional field); after contains precisely the same field keys. Do not alter other fields. A new position keeps region, anchor_entity, relation, certain and reference_frame="image". A spatial_relations entry has axis, anchor_entity, reference_frame="image", subject_part, anchor_part, relation, certain, support and evidence_refs. Allowed axes/relations: horizontal=image_left_of/image_right_of/overlapping/uncertain; vertical=above/below/overlapping/uncertain; contact=touching/on/inside/none/uncertain. Anchor IDs must exist in the preserved inventory. Unknown facts use uncertainty, not a negative fact.
Preserve already supported observations and uncertainties. Correct a materially false free-text claim as well as its typed relation, so the package is coherent. Do not silently erase task-relevant evidence or add unsupported replacement claims. Omit updates to unchanged entities. Every update needs a concrete image reason and exactly ["${frame_id}_IMAGE"]. unchanged_entity_ids lists all non-updated original IDs in original order. entity_checks lists exactly the focus IDs in supplied order with status preserve/patch/uncertain and a concrete reason. Unchanged background remains a hypothesis for complete Gate C review; this patch does not grant approval.
If the image cannot establish a coherent repair, return status hold, no updates, all IDs unchanged and explain uncertainty. A hold is a valid semantic result. Otherwise status patched requires at least one update, or unchanged requires no updates.

{"frame_id":"$frame_id","source_observation_sha256":"$source_sha256","status":"patched|unchanged|hold","entity_checks":[{"entity_id":"actual focus ID","status":"preserve|patch|uncertain","reason":"visible support or uncertainty"}],"entity_updates":[{"entity_id":"actual focus ID","before":{"visible_state":"exact original value"},"after":{"visible_state":"image-grounded replacement"},"reason":"concrete visible comparison","evidence_refs":["${frame_id}_IMAGE"]}],"frame_updates":[],"unchanged_entity_ids":[],"uncertainties":[]}
The example update is schema illustration, not a required answer. Use actual IDs and exact before values.

Conversely mere proximity without such cues does not establish a hold.
Use above/over/left/right for grounded image-plane placement unless the wording explicitly asserts physical depth or contact. Qualitative relations and explicitly approximate image estimates do not require measured annotations. Check the estimate's broad consistency; do not treat approximate as exact.
